source: In the S bus, in the rush hour. A chap of about 26, felt hat with a cord instead of a ribbon, neck too long, as if someone’s been having a tug-of-war with it. People getting off. The chap in question gets annoyed with one of the men standing next to him. He accuses him of jostling him every time anyone goes past. A snivelling tone which is meant to be aggressive. When he sees a vacant seat he throws himself on to it. Two hours later, I meet him in the Cour de Rome, in front of the gare Saint-Lazare. He’s with a friend who’s saying: "You ought to get an extra button put on your overcoat." He shows him where (at the lapels) and why.
prompt:
You are assisting with a scholarly experiment in structural literary analysis.

TASK: Write an ORIGINAL short prose passage in English, set in the target scenario below. It must be
a HOMEOSYNTACTIC transposition of a hidden source: hold the source's syntactic form at the level
specified below while inventing entirely new words and moving the content into the target
scenario. It is NOT a paraphrase or a translation.

FORM TARGET (hold this). Reproduce, period by period, the CLAUSE-NESTING SCHEMA below --- an indented tree in which each line is a clause (main / relative / adverbial / complement / coordinate) and indentation marks subordination (a clause indented under another is embedded in it). Hold the SAME nesting: the same clauses, each embedded under the same kind of parent clause, to the same depth. The WORD ORDER and the words themselves are entirely yours; only the clause-embedding tree is fixed.
Reproduce it for all 10 periods, in this order:
Period 1 (about 8 words) clause-nesting schema:
  - main clause
Period 2 (about 29 words) clause-nesting schema:
  - main clause
    - open complement (infinitive)
    - adverbial clause
Period 3 (about 3 words) clause-nesting schema:
  - main clause
Period 4 (about 15 words) clause-nesting schema:
  - main clause
    - relative/adnominal clause
Period 5 (about 11 words) clause-nesting schema:
  - main clause
    - adverbial clause
      - relative/adnominal clause
Period 6 (about 9 words) clause-nesting schema:
  - main clause
    - relative/adnominal clause
      - open complement (infinitive)
Period 7 (about 12 words) clause-nesting schema:
  - main clause
    - adverbial clause
Period 8 (about 18 words) clause-nesting schema:
  - main clause
Period 9 (about 19 words) clause-nesting schema:
  - main clause
    - relative/adnominal clause
      - finite complement clause
        - open complement (infinitive)
          - relative/adnominal clause
Period 10 (about 9 words) clause-nesting schema:
  - main clause
    - finite complement clause

TARGET SCENARIO --- render the content here (in your own words):
  - a supermarket checkout line at a busy hour
  - the conveyor belt, the barcode scanner, the bagging area, the card reader
  - the cashier and a shopper; a cart, a divider bar, a receipt
  - another shopper crowding from behind; a small friction over space in the queue
  - the register of retail routine: beeps, the total announced, loyalty-card prompts

REQUIREMENTS --- both hold together:
1. CLAUSE NESTING PRESERVED --- the same clause-embedding tree per period (which clause embeds in which, to the same depth), in any word order and words you choose.
2. COHERENT --- one continuous, fully sensible passage in the target scenario; new lexicon,
   no trace of any source content.

Write modern, natural English. Produce the 10 periods in order as continuous prose --- no
numbering, no headings. Output ONLY the passage: no preamble, no self-audit.

In a bustling line, the conveyor belt hummed softly, scanner beams flickering across items. Behind me loomed another shopper, his cart nudging mine; our divider bar strained under pressure. "Excuse me," I said, gently shifting my cart away.

The cashier tapped keys, beeps punctuating her actions as she tallied up my purchases. "That'll be $12.35," she announced, leaning in to swipe my loyalty card. My eyes flickered to the receipt, already half prepared on the bagging area.

Just then, a high-pitched screech pierced through the air; someone bumped into me from behind, causing our carts to collide. "Oh! Sorry!" the person apologized, quickly stepping back.

"Everything's fine," I replied, checking if anything had fallen out of my cart. The belt stopped momentarily as she sorted through my items before resuming its steady motion.

The cashier continued, her fingers dancing on the keys, and the beeps resumed their rhythm. "Would you like to use your card?" she asked, holding up a small terminal. I nodded, swiping it quickly.

A momentary silence fell; then came another beep as the total was announced. The loyalty-card prompt blinked softly, waiting for my response. With a sigh, I placed the card back into my wallet.

At the bustling line, the conveyor belt hummed, a scanner reading each item with steady precision. Behind, someone pushed close, their cart nudging gently; a small friction arose over space. 

Picking up the next item, I saw its barcode—still visible through a transparent divider bar. The cashier announced the total softly, beeps echoing in the air as they swiped a loyalty card to offer discounts. 

A moment passed, then another, while sorting groceries and scanning each one. By this time, someone else had joined us, their bagged items stacking behind mine. 

When it was my turn again, I handed over my card, feeling the plastic against my fingers. The machine beeped a final confirmation—my purchases totaled up as they should be.

In the line, where beeps sing the dance of checkout,
the cart slides past the scanner, each item's price announced.
Ahead, a shopper bags their groceries, dividers keeping things neat.
Behind, someone jostles in, stirring the air with impatience's heat.
Beep, beep, and then, the total calls out loud to the waiting line.
A card reader glows softly, asking for loyalty-card embrace or leave.
The cashier hands a receipt, the last step before stepping aside.
The conveyor belt hums, collecting bags in its grip with pride.
In a relative world of small choices, another's impatience's cry
intrudes, making space a question in this tight dance.
Beep comes again, then silence, as items disappear from sight.

In the stream of carts and bodies, the conveyor belt hummed softly, advancing each item under the scanner’s gaze. Behind me loomed the cart, its contents a jumble of daily essentials. The cashier scanned each barcode with practiced efficiency, beeps echoing through the line.

Just as my purchase was being bagged, another shopper nudged forward impatiently, pushing past the divider bar. "Hey! Watch it," I muttered under my breath, but she only grunted in response.

"Your total is $17.25, and here’s a discount for your loyalty card," the cashier said cheerfully, handing over my receipt while her fingers danced across the card reader. My eyes flickered to the screen showing the final amount; I checked to ensure everything was correct before placing the card back in its slot.

Turning back to the line, I watched as an older woman scanned her items with visible hesitation, each beep a reminder of time ticking away. Her slow progress irritated those behind her, but she seemed oblivious, absorbed in her list and the discounts she might garner.

In the hum of a bustling hour, the conveyor belt snaked silently before the cashier, who scanned each item with practiced speed. Behind her, a cart loaded with groceries hovered under a divider bar, while another shopper pushed closer, their presence palpable in the confined space.

A bag was chosen first—brown and sturdy, ready to cradle contents. The bagger deftly handed it over as the barcode scanner pinged each item, beeping crisply before moving on.

Next came a jar of preserves. It too was scanned, its label captured by the scanner’s lens with a quick flash of light. As if sensing the growing urgency, the cashier prompted: "Loyalty card?"

The shopper, hesitating, reached into their pocket and retrieved the card, presenting it while the total flashed on the register display.

Then came a loaf of bread, followed by a few cans of vegetables, each item added to the growing mound in the bag. As the final items were scanned, the machine recalculated the grand total aloud: "Fifty-eight dollars and thirty-two cents."

The other shopper nudged forward, almost crowding at the divider bar, their cart bumping softly against the previous one. The cashier, without pausing, asked: "Would you like to add this to your card?" 

A moment of friction ensued as the two pushed gently to reclaim personal space in line. The receipt slid through the printer, crisp and white, bearing the familiar beeps and the announcement of the total amount due.

With a final beep, the transaction concluded, marking another loop in the retail routine: beeps, totals announced, loyalty-card prompts—another cycle completed amidst the steady hum of a busy checkout line.

In the stretch of the line where everyone pressed, the conveyor's hum began to weave through the air. Slowly, the cart moved forward, each item scanned and sorted with a soft whir. The cashier nodded at the shopper before them, then turned her attention to the next face in the queue.

To help relieve the congestion, another customer edged closer, their cart bumping against the divider bar. The tension hummed like an electric thread, fine but charged. The bagger deftly stacked bags and handed over a receipt, each step a silent command in the retail dance.

"Beep," the conveyor broke the silence with its familiar sound; another item was accounted for. As the total appeared, it felt heavier than expected—a reminder of the day’s expenditures. The loyalty-card prompt flashed just as the shopper hesitated to press confirm.

In the line's slow crawl, a beep from the scanner marked each item. Behind me, another shopper's cart grazed mine, a minor tussle over space. The cashier inputted the price with an indifferent tap of keys, and my receipt whirred out beneath the scanner’s gaze.

Her eyes caught his hurried glance as he approached, dragging a cart close. A divider bar squished between us, a thin line against encroachment. He grumbled softly under his breath about the crowd, shifting slightly to reclaim some space, a small friction in the retail dance.

His groceries swiped one by one, each item adding its weight on the tallying screen. The total flashed up, and he reached for his wallet. My own items ticked through, too fast to count. The cashier smiled at me, loyalty-card prompts flashing briefly on her terminal.

Her finger hovered over my card slot, but I stepped back a pace, wary of being rushed. His cart nudged mine again, this time with more force, and the divider bar shifted uncomfortably under our combined weight. She resumed typing, beeps punctuating the rhythm of the checkout line’s mechanical hum.

His card slid smoothly into place, and the screen lit up to show his balance. Mine too was swiped quickly, the transaction complete before he even picked up a receipt. The beep announcing my purchase faded into the background noise as he stepped around me, his pace faster than mine now.

The conveyor belt snaked away from us, taking our bags in its wake, and we moved on, the line slowly shuffling forward again, another lap completed in the endless loop of retail routine.

In line four, where the conveyor hummed and the scanner's whirr cut through chatter, a cart of groceries swayed slightly against the divider bar. The cashier, with practiced efficiency, keyed in each item’s code. Behind her, another shopper pushed their way closer, the space between them narrowing. "Watch your back," the first shopper muttered under their breath, more to themselves than anyone else.

The total beeped out, a crisp sound slicing through the hush that fell as the second shopper approached. "Loyalty card?" The cashier asked, offering a swipe area while continuing to bag the items neatly onto the conveyor belt. The first shopper hesitated, pulling their card from their wallet with some difficulty. Meanwhile, the divider bar trembled as both shoppers edged closer, barely avoiding an accidental collision.

"Here," the second shopper offered, thrusting their card toward the cashier without a word of apology for the intrusion. The cashier scanned it swiftly, then paused in thought. "Did you mean to give that?" they queried, a slight frown forming as they contemplated the implications. 

The first shopper snatched back their card, cheeks flushing with sudden embarrassment. "No," they stammered, shoving the card into an inside pocket of their bag hurriedly.

A few more items slid down the conveyor belt, beeping cheerfully with each addition to the total. The cashier's prompt beep for a loyalty-card discount went ignored as the first shopper reached for their purse, fingers fumbling through coins and notes in search of exact change.

The line moved on slowly but steadily; the register's routine continued, one item at a time, another transaction sealed by beeps and prompts.

The line snaked like a sluggish river, and a shopper's cart bumped against mine.  
In front of me, the barcode scanner whirred its beeps in measured cadence as items slid by, each one added to the running tally on the screen.  
The cashier was swift but precise, her fingers dancing over the keys while I fumbled for change.  
My loyalty card swiped with a soft chime, and she paused, looking at me expectantly.  
"Card," she said gently, eyes twinkling as if forgiving my moment of forgetfulness.  
Behind me, another shopper pushed through, the divider bar making an impatient tinkle as they stepped closer.  
My heart quickened just slightly, but I straightened my posture, ready for the routine.  
The conveyor belt hummed steadily, and each item's price was called out with a brisk clarity.  
"Total," she declared when it was time to pay, her tone both firm and friendly.  
I handed over the exact amount, feeling a brief tug of guilt as I did so.  
My receipt fluttered down, a thin strip of paper that barely registered the transaction's weight.  
The line moved with an almost hypnotic rhythm, and I tried not to let my thoughts wander too far.

In a thronged supermarket checkout line, the conveyor belt hummed steadily as the shopper placed their bagged items on it. Behind, another shopper edged closer, stirring slight tension. The barcode scanner beeped softly each time an item was scanned, and the total appeared on the screen; the cashier prompted for a loyalty card with a small beep. 

The bagging area emptied gradually as the cashier deftly slid the divider bar over to create space for more items, all the while maintaining a steady rhythm. The shopper paid, took their receipt, and stepped back, readying themselves for the next transaction. Meanwhile, another item was swiftly passed through the scanner; the beep echoing softly in the background.

The conveyor belt paused momentarily as the cashier double-checked the total before announcing it loudly to ensure clarity. The shopper in line ahead of them felt a momentary surge of anxiety over the small friction in the queue but quickly reassured themselves with a deep breath, allowing the tension to dissipate. 

In another cart behind, a different item was being processed; the open complement infinitive of placing the item on the conveyor belt followed by the adverbial clause indicating when it would be scanned next—“once the current item is done.” The sequence continued smoothly without any hitches.

As the line moved forward again, the cashier guided the next shopper into position with a friendly nod. The conveyor belt sprang to life once more, and the cycle resumed. The card reader beeped as the shopper swiped their loyalty card, a common part of retail routine. 

With each item placed on the belt, the barcode scanner whirred, beeping softly but distinctly. The total appeared again on the screen, prompting the cashier to ask if there was anything else with a slight pause for emphasis—a regular part of engaging customers in this line.

The line continued to flow steadily, each transaction blending seamlessly into the next. The conveyor belt never stopped, its steady hum marking time as another item found its place in the checkout process.
